assets.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: ONE simplified in-game hero sprite design for a Java top-down 2D action RPG.
Edit target/reference: provided six-pose brown-haired hero sheet. Preserve the character identity, but redraw ONLY a single front-facing idle hero with empty hands. No other views, no sheet, no labels.
Primary request: genuinely coarse, disciplined low-resolution pixel-art visual language. This is a radical reduction of texture detail, not a polished illustration with a pixel filter. Match the readability and restrained detail density of well-crafted small indie RPG sprites. Original design; do not copy a named game character.
Design: same warm brown swept hair, red scarf with a short tail flowing right, navy short tunic, cream rolled cuffs, dark trousers, simple brown belt with one small brass buckle, brown boots, two clearly separate empty hands. Compact adventurous young hero, roughly 3 heads tall. Head larger relative to body than reference. Retain cheerful determined character.
Shape simplification: hair is 4 or 5 large coherent locks, only 3 brown tones; scarf one red body, one dark red shadow, one small red highlight; tunic only 3 navy tones; each boot is a single readable chunky silhouette with ONE cuff, no laces; one diagonal leather strap, no dangling pouches. No fabric weave, individual hair strands, metal speculars, jewelry, micro folds or rim glow.
Pixel structure: compose on a conceptual 48 columns by 64 rows logical canvas; figure approximately 30 pixels wide by 52 pixels tall, centered, feet on the same horizontal baseline with free transparent margin. Enlarge the logical pixels as exact uniform square blocks with nearest-neighbor appearance. Every contour should step on this ONE coarse grid. No small pixels nested inside larger pixels. No smooth curves, NO anti-aliasing, NO gradients, NO dithering, no semi-transparent edge, no texture, no illustration shading.
Palette: transparent + these opaque colors ONLY: #171c2b #303544 #4c342f #79513a #b17b4c #dda965 #9b654c #dca070 #f3c895 #4b2431 #922f42 #d14d4d #ef8863 #172e46 #294762 #496981 #72765f #afa987 #e4d2a0 #413932 #74523c #ae8051 #be9458 #f4e5c4. Use distinct flat colored pixel clusters.
Composition: one character alone, front-facing with a slight top-down game view, symmetrical resting feet, arms relaxed apart from torso, fully visible silhouette. Genuinely transparent background and NO cast shadow, NO ground, NO glow, NO checkerboard painted into the image.
The output is meant to be inspected at tiny game display sizes, not to maximize detail at full size. Favor clean flat clusters and silhouette.

Use case: style-transfer.
Edit target: the provided sealed holy sword concept. Create one radically simplified low-resolution pixel-art sword, same identity, tilted exactly 45 degrees from lower left handle to upper right tip.
Preserve ivory straight blade, dark bronze seal bands, plain muted gold guard, brown grip. Reduce three intricate chain loops to TWO bold flat dark bands around the blade, each represented by a few broad pixel clusters. Simplify the guard into a short straight crossguard with a tiny ochre center square. Remove gem reflections, bevels, engraved borders, tiny chain links and distressed metal. Blade has a broad pale face and one grey shadow plane; 3 tones total. Grip is a single dark brown bar with just one light stripe. No aura, glow, particles, cast shadow, background or text.
Design it as a coherent small game item on a 32 by 32 logical pixel grid, enlarged into perfectly uniform square pixel blocks with nearest-neighbor appearance. Important: coarse pixel clusters, no thin subpixel details, no antialiasing, no gradient, no texture. Maximum 12 FLAT visible colors, genuinely transparent background, hard opaque edges. Entire sword fits inside canvas with 2-pixel transparent margin. Handle near (6,26), point near (28,3). Silhouette should still clearly read as a sealed sacred straight sword when shown only 48 to 64 screen pixels tall. Single separate asset, not a sheet, not a scene. The desired result is restrained game-ready visual language, not a luxurious inventory illustration.

nativeSource.method: Independently authored character-per-pixel source in the existing Art.java text grammar. No generated PNG is used as input to the source builder or Java exporter.
